newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Finance Minister fails to cure India woes.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Finance Minister fails to cure India woes.

text.p: Continued delays in a speech by Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram and the expectation that when it does come, there will not be much in it, depressed Indian global depositary receipt prices in London.
"There is a complete lack of interest in this market," said one trader.

Investors and Indian corporates had been looking for relief from minimum company tax levels, but hopes have diminished as the finance minister's speech to give effect to budget proposals has been delayed since last week and in any case, Chidambaram launched a defence of the "minimum alternate tax" yesterday.

The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR Index JCEAI fell 1.89 points, or 2.62 percent to 70.49 points, a premium of 11.25 percent over the local market after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index fell 33.46 points, 0.96 percent, 3,434.83.
Elswhere in Asia, Taiwan remained weak as a territory dispute with Japan over an island chain simmered.

The Capel Taiwan index fell 1.52 points, 1.67 percent to 89.23 points, a premium of 3.07 percent over the local market after the Taiwan Weighted Index The weighted index lost 19.67 points or 0.31 percent to finish at 6,415.76.

Korean depositary receipts picked up on the back of a strong performance from Samsung after expectations that the key U.S. Semiconductor Industry Association would report an improved book to bill ratio of orders to shipments.
Analysts are looking for a ratio of between 0.86 and 0.92, up from 0.85 in July and the figures will be released later on Tuesday.
Samsung global depositary shares rose $1.25 to $21.00/22.00 after the local stock rose 3,300 won, or 5.79 percent, to 60,300 won.
LG Electronics GDS rose 28 cents to $5.90/$6.25 after the local gained 800 won, or 5.71 percent, to its upper limit of 14,800.
This helped propel the Capel Korea Index up 1.77 points, 2.64 percent to 68.68 points, a premium of 22.04 percent over the local market, wich closed up 5.66 points at 803.04.
